body: It is also quite confusing to have 3 possible results.

Problem has two sides:
1. i have to convert `null` to empty string to auto select current option
2. i have to convert empty string to `null` to set correct value

it means that i have to write many if's in `[ngModel]` and `(ngModelChange)`.

body:
Yes, this is a very annoying problem for us! having null in ngValue would be so useful!

Currently we have to do a lot of extra work to deal with nulls, just like @kemsky has stated above.

It looks like @kb3eua may have fixed this problem for a future release?

**I'm submitting a ...**  (check one with "x")

```
[x] bug report
```

**Current behavior**

```
<select id="idState" name="state" [ngModel]="user?.state"  
(ngModelChange)="user==null || user.state=$event">
       <option value="">N/A - 1</option>
       <option [ngValue]="">N/A - 2</option>
       <option [ngValue]="null">N/A - 3</option>
       <option *ngFor="let s of states"  
[ngValue]="s">{{s.shortName}}</option>
</select>
```

I can not set `user.state` to `null`:
N/A - 1 produce empty string
N/A - 2 produce "N/A - 2"
N/A - 3 produce "0: null"

**Expected/desired behavior**

Should be able to set `null`.

**What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior?**

I don't want to clean up values manually for every nullable field.

issue.title: Undefined can't be used as ngValue for select option without extra treatment
issue.body:
**I'm submitting a ...**
- [x] bug report
- [ ] feature request
- [ ] support request => Please do not submit support request here, see note at the top of this template.

**Current behavior**
`undefined` or `null` value can't be used as `ngValue` for a select option.

**Expected/desired behavior**
Ability to use `undefined` or `null` value as `ngValue` for a select option without workaround shown in the reproduction below.

[Steps to reproduce and a minimal demo of the problem](http://plnkr.co/59brW0sOKSfUduojBUpm).

**_My investigations**_
Currently in [`_getOptionValue`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/6da79673c207b41b117737dcfcb302d17a0fb8ab/modules/%40angular/common/src/forms/directives/select_control_value_accessor.ts#L90-L93) function the fact that the key is not present in the map of options and the fact that the value for an existing key is undefined are treated the same. But only the former case should be treated like it's done currently, when the key is present in the map of options the corresponding value should be returned regardless of what it is.

```
[x ] bug report
[ ] feature request
[ ] support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
```

**Current behavior**
When setting the initial value of a `<select>` control to either null or undefined, the rendered `<select>` element displays the first `<option>`.

**Expected/desired behavior**
If the value of the Control is set to null, undefined or to a value not found in the list of options, the rendered element should displays an empty select.

**Reproduction of the problem**
Here is a plnkr: 
[http://plnkr.co/edit/7aHyWPt41YdvQH09MH8x?p=preview](http://plnkr.co/edit/7aHyWPt41YdvQH09MH8x?p=preview)

**What is the expected behavior?**
The current behavior found on Chrome and Firefox are the expected behavior.

**What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior?**
The `<select>` element that is rendered should not display a selected option if the model backing it is not set to the value of that option.

**Please tell us about your environment:**
- **Angular version:** 2.0.0-rc.4
- **Browser:** IE 11 & Edge 25
- **Language:** TypeScript 1.8.10
